# Octatrack (MKI, MKII): agent context pack

Data checked 2026-11-14, research snapshot `a1b74d9c7699`. Generated from the Aggregat database; every item links back to the Markdown that is the source of truth. Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. Evidence: `[hw]` seen on a real unit, `[emu]` emulator only, `[doc]` stated without a test result, `[?]` unclear or inferred.

Full version. The brief one is [octatrack-brief.md](octatrack-brief.md).

## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]
- **A57** On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. [hw]
- **A58** A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. [hw]
- **A59** Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. [hw]
- **A60** Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. [hw]
- **A61** Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). [doc]
- **A62** When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. [hw]
- **A63** When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. [hw]
- **A64** When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Octatrack (MKI, MKII)

- **C4** (C) Emulators do not prove real-time DSP behaviour. The earlier digikit README said "no audio"; the current ElekLabs Features that cross the ColdFire-SHARC boundary need both processors emulated together, or a unit: dn2mk2's BOUNCE passed a ColdFire-only gate and failed on units. On the Octatrack the DSP AMP envelope restart only showed as clicks on a unit. Incidents: [I58](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i58-a-wavetable-machine-clicked-on-every-note), [I66](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i66-a-feature-that-crosses-coldfire-and-dsp-passed-the-gate-and-failed-on-units). README has ColdFire + SHARC+ running together with audio, but the DSP "does not run in real time yet", and dn2mk2 reports the emulators do not model the two chips' timing. DSP overruns show up only on a unit. `[doc]` {digikit-old} Incidents: [I36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x).
- **C9** (C) After every install, open a project saved before it, and install the next build over the normal route. Old data meets new code only on the unit: a DN2 project with a stored row count out of range crashed stock and modded builds, Octatrack projects stalled when an effect layout changed, dn2mk2's MD/MM tracks went silent after an install, armio's USB audio repeated after a project change, and Overtone 1.0 broke the next USB update. A release test opens an old project and a stock project, changes project once, and installs the following build with Transfer. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I13](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i13-usb-audio-repeated-old-audio-after-a-project-change), [I21](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i21-md-and-monomachine-tracks-went-silent-after-an-install), [I22](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path), [I28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). [I73](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i73-an-old-project-stopped-all-sound-on-a-sample-machine-mod) (an old project silenced every track), [I77](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i77-knob-assignments-a-mod-kept-in-a-kits-spare-bytes-were-lost-at-power-on) (mod data lost at a cold boot after SAVE PROJECT). `[hw]`
- **C12** (C) Before you blame your mod, check [STOCK-BUGS.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/STOCK-BUGS.md) and reproduce the misbehaviour on the unmodified OS with the same steps; a stock bug you find goes into that list. The reverse holds too: before you call it a stock fault, check that your own watchdog does not mistake one of stock's deliberate pauses for a fault - Modwerk's Octatrack base read the DSP pause of USB DISK MODE as a stall ([I69](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i69-a-mod-took-stocks-usb-disk-mode-pause-for-a-dsp-stall-and-kept-the-audio-off)). Mods reach stock paths, and stock paths have bugs: a Part change by a mod shows the Octatrack's carry-over bug exactly as a stock pattern change does, and a damaged project halts stock and modded Digitone II builds alike. Record a new stock bug with the device and OS, the trigger, the cause if known and how it was found, and your workaround. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject} {kyoti-bugfixes}
- **E3** (E) Keep every stored count and select value in range, and stamp old projects after a layout change. Stock trusts what it loads: the DN2's song LOAD copies a stored row count without a check (21,503 rows instead of at most 99 crashed stock and modded builds alike), and an Octatrack select value outside its count stalled the sequencer on first play after an effect's layout changed. Clamp every count and enum a mod writes; when a build changes a stored layout, rewrite old projects' values on load. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject}

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [doc] Other Elektron devices, from elekloader's BUILDING.md (for reference): Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII - FUNC at power-on (STARTUP menu), TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over 5-pin DIN MIDI, USB does not work. Octatrack - hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE, DIN MIDI; normal flashing from the card (PROJECT > SYSTEM > USB DISK MODE, copy the `.bin`, then PROJECT > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE, power-cycle once more before judging). Digitakt mk1 / Digitone mk1: FUNC, TRIG 4, legacy mode; the connection is not stated for these two. Per-device notes: [`analog-rytm.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md), [`digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md), [`digitone.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-building} (`recovery#ff8f0917`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L37))

## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB7** EP0 data stages of a multiple of 64 bytes stall or freeze (Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C; stock behaviour). Workaround: size replies a byte short, or clear ZLT when priming.
- **SB8** About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered (Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C; stock behaviour). Workaround: finish a completed stage from a 60 Hz tick, or stall EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits.
- **SB9** A Plays-Free MIDI track stalls after its first step (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by octatrack-kyoti-fw's BATCH_BUGFIXES (`MIDI_PLAYS_FREE_FIX`); hardware-confirmed 2026-08-28.
- **SB10** A pattern that holds only parameter locks shows as empty (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by BATCH_BUGFIXES (`EMPTY_PATTERN_LED_FIX`) under [PTN]; under [BANK] it stays as stock, because scanning 256 patterns' locks on every LED refresh starved the CPU.
- **SB11** A pattern-triggered Part change carries the old Part's state over (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by BATCH_BUGFIXES (`PART_CHANGE_CARRYOVER_FIX`): republish the recorder records, set the voice-kill bit, re-seed the slot.
- **SB12** A trigless lock stays lit after its last lock is erased (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by octatrack-kyoti-fw's ERASE_EMPTY_TRIGLESS_LOCKS (a deliberately empty trigless lock placed with FUNC + TRIG is left alone).
- **SB13** LO-FI's AMF ring-mod pitch falls at eleven values instead of rising (Octatrack MKI and MKII, OS 1.40C (LO-FI on FX1 and FX2); open in stock; fixed by a mod (not yet run on hardware per the Modwerk draft)). Workaround: `mpyuu` instead (octa-bt-pt's LOFI AMF FIX; also a Modwerk draft module). Saved projects at affected values will sound different with the fix.
- **SB14** Probable: SPATIALIZER's ring misaligns when selected mid-play (Octatrack, OS 1.40C; unconfirmed). Workaround: none yet; the source plans a hardware test on stock.
- **SB17** The AUDIO EDITOR key opens the sample the track had before (Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: reselect the track first; fixed by OCTAMAX 2f.
- **SB22** One Part byte outside its stock range drops the whole bank at power-on (Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C; stock behaviour). Workaround: store only values stock accepts in stock records (rule A60).

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I5** EP0 data stages of a multiple of 64 bytes stall or freeze (stock USB driver). Cause: stock leaves zero-length termination on in the EP0 OUT queue head. Fix: size replies a byte short, or clear ZLT when priming. Rules: A39.
- **I6** About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered. Cause: the stage completes inside the ISR after stock's poll, or stops part-way. Fix: a 60 Hz tick finishes a completed stage, or stalls EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits. Rules: A39.
- **I7** A soft reset leaves the USB controller running. Cause: the controller and PHY keep their state over a soft reset. Fix: stop the controller (USBCMD.RS = 0), wait ~50 ms, then reset; 20 of 20 good boots. Rules: A40.
- **I28** A select value outside its count stalled the sequencer. Cause: stored values no longer fit the new layout. Fix: stamp old projects' stored values after a layout change. Rules: E3,C9.
- **I29** DSP scratch at `$84` and up hung the unit. Cause: r7 scratch `$00-$83` is the per-instance block; above it belongs to others. Fix: stay inside the per-instance block. Rules: D11.
- **I30** Key events posted into stock's queues crashed the unit minutes later. Cause: events posted straight into stock's internal queues. Fix: feed the panel parser its own bytes instead. Rules: A50.
- **I31** Restoring DSP-read state every frame corrupted the audio. Cause: a mod overwrote data the DSP reads each frame; doing so is safe only for CPU-side bookkeeping. Fix: restore only CPU-side state. Rules: A50.
- **I32** A DSP frame counter saturated after 50.7 minutes. Cause: a counter past `$7fffff` saturates in `move a,nN`. Fix: mask counters to 23 bits. Rules: A51.
- **I33** Module state on a load-meter counter gave a jittery pitch. Cause: module state at `X:$2840`, core 1's load-meter counter. Fix: move the state. Rules: D11.
- **I34** A startup change stalled at the logo after a long power-off. Cause: unknown; keeping the activation helper resident fixed it. Fix: qualify startup changes after a long power-off. Rules: A40.
- **I35** USB replies stayed stale for minutes. Cause: DMA reads RAM, not the copyback cache. Fix: copy a reply through the uncached alias and send it from there. Rules: A48,A28.
- **I48** A menu table in a "free" zero run crashed the unit. Cause: the 15 KB zero run at `0x401087e4` lies in the PROJECT subsystem's RAM (the zero region above `0x400d8000`). Fix: larger code goes to a loader-copied area (octabam's loader stub at `0x4010fdf0`). Rules: D11,A43.
- **I57** A demand-loader soak froze an Octatrack MKII. Cause: the demand loader's BASE/MODULATION transition is the larger factor (only the loader changed between the two images, and the rate fell from about 1 in 6 to 1 in 118); STEM REC and its 18 MiB reserve are not cleared. Candidate for the total freeze: two waits in the frame interrupt with no time limit (the loader's wait before each host word, and stock's spin until the DSP takes the frame's host command). Fix: partial (one copy per load). Time limits on the waits and copying a slice per frame are proposed, not made. Rules: A51,A29.
- **I58** A wavetable machine clicked on every note. Cause: the DSP's AMP envelope restarts from zero at every trig START; with any ATK above 0 a sound that keeps playing across trigs drops to silence and fades back in. Fix: hold the DSP at ATK 0 / HOLD INF / REL INF and shape AMP in the machine, as SYNTH MACHINE does (W5). Rules: C4.
- **I59** Patch state inside a stock task's buffer silenced tracks. Cause: patch state at `0x80006a00-0x80007000` lay inside the work buffer of the stock audio-analysis task (`0x80006964-0x80007574`). The crash is not proven to come from this. Fix: OCTAMAX_2h keeps all patch state in DDR; the build refuses any operand that points into the buffer. Rules: A43,A50.
- **I60** A long copy with interrupts masked clicked on every reload. Cause: a 43 KB pattern copy ran with interrupts masked and held off the audio frame. Fix: copy with interrupts on and publish only the slices that changed. Also fixed in the same round: reloading the current pattern while another was cued let the cued one land anyway. Rules: A34.
- **I69** A mod took stock's USB DISK MODE pause for a DSP stall and kept the audio off. Cause: stock pauses the DSP while USB DISK MODE is open. The base's stall watch read that pause as a stalled DSP, and its recovery held the audio stopped. It was never reproduced on a stock unit. Fix: the base tells that pause from a stall (2026-11-10); on the owner's MKII the walk, about 10 s in the mode, NO and PLAY now plays. Rules: C12.
- **I72** A drum machine mod played silent hits after power-up and misread stock's voice start. Cause: the hit level was scaled from a base read only when a restore bit at `0x80001538` was clear, and on the unit that bit can be set at power-up, so the base stayed 0. Separately, the mod's wrapper of the FLEX voice start passed two arguments where stock's routine `0x4000f450(track, slot, flags)` takes three, so stock read a word of the wrapper's stack. Fix: the base is now the lane's VOL; the wrapper forwards all three arguments, and stock's retrigs run. Rules: G8,C10.
- **I75** Removing a synth module that tracks still used left the loader stuck in recovery. Cause: not traced in the source; the module's README now says to remove it only while no track in the Part uses it. Fix: a power cycle brought the unit back. Rules: A54.
- **I78** The first PLAY after power-on started a track's recorder. Cause: a quantized REC start left staged at `0x800018be`/`0x800018de` (the QREC branch of REC_POST `0x40005178`). Whether stock alone does this is unclear. Fix: FREE LOOP's `stray_guard` stops such a recording; not seen on images 42-43. Rules: A40,G8.
- **I79** Three FM Synth tracks beside a busy pattern froze an Octatrack. Cause: the CPU-rendered machines were not counted against any budget, so nothing stopped the load from passing the frame (measured by the fix, not traced further). Fix: the base prices each CPU machine, refuses a pick over the limit (CPU FULL) and drops voices at the frame guard; the same set then played on a development build. A busy project may now drop FM Synth notes. Rules: A25,A34.
- **I82** A frame interrupt entering about 150 µs late stopped an Octatrack's DSP frame exchange. Cause: at START and at a program change one frame interrupt runs 475-585 µs (a frame is 362.8 µs), so the next one enters late. A log of entry times showed: 128-149 µs late, the unit catches up; 155-223 µs late, it skips one frame and runs on; both stalls entered 149 and 155 µs late. A USB capture adds 25-30 µs to the START frame and moved it onto that boundary; adding 60 µs to every frame interrupt without a capture moved it past and caused no stall. Inferred: the ColdFire's transfer chain is still sending when the DSP starts its next frame. Fix: octabam's FRAME GUARD holds an entry 110-190 µs late until it is 190 µs late, so the DSP skips one frame cleanly; with it 32 first STARTs and 192 program changes ran without a stall at 20 channels. A first version mis-reduced the lateness after a skip and still stalled in a long program-change soak; corrected 2026-11-13. Not measured: what the skipped frame does to sounding audio; an MKI. Rules: A56.
- **I83** Reading the CF card from a mod's UI tick froze an Octatrack. Cause: the player read the card from AERIA's UI tick; stock does its card work in its own card task. Fix: v32 switched the player off (plan: read in the card task, or preload the file into RAM); starting the screensaver no longer stalls. Rules: A57.
- **I85** A delay effect left the next effect in its DSP slot silent. Cause: moving PT2399 to another block of core 1's X memory (`X:$2000`) stopped it. Fix: a build that survived 12 rounds of the trigger and 30 random swaps; PT2399 shares memory with BBD, HAIL and AURORA, so those pairs are refused; BBD removed in v0.9.3. Rules: A58.
- **I86** An own engine filled the output half that was about to play: late samples on the analog outputs only. Cause: the engine wrote into the half of its output DMA buffer that was about to play. Fix: the engine fills the other half; noise through the loop then arrived with one delay at all 16 positions. Rules: A58.
- **I95** One byte a mod stored made stock drop a whole Octatrack bank at restart. Cause: VECTOR packed SPAN into a byte's top bits, so SPAN 8-12 stored 0x80 or more; stock's Part check counts that as bad, and at boot the battery restore runs before the base has its modules back, so VECTOR's wrapper around the check did not apply (SB22). Fix: 0.3.2 moves SPAN's top bit to a free bit of the next byte and rewrites old bytes; the bank stayed intact on restart. Rules: A60,E3.
- **I96** Every effect pick was refused with NO ROOM after a restart. Cause: a restore makes all modules live in one pass and the board binds Sidechain's key-bus slot on a later tick, so Air Chorus's buffer took the block before the key bus was counted and every later pick failed. Fix: the base counts live controllers that no slot holds yet; host-tested only. Rules: G8.
- **I84** Uninitialised shared-window memory crashed DSP core 1 on a cold boot; the emulator starts it at zero. Cause: core 1's slot table in the shared window held random values at power-on; the emulator zeroes that memory. Fix: core 1 clears its table before it starts. Rules: C10.
- **I76** A loader base update over USB said Done but did not stick. Cause: unknown. Fix: update again and check the base version after the reboot. Rules: A23.
- **I100** A Windows PC could not open the Octatrack's vendor interface. Cause: Windows writes that value only at an interface's first setup; why it was missing on members' PCs is unknown. Fix: the base reports `bcdDevice` 0x0101, which made Windows write the value again. Rules: A63.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O22** Has octabam's WAVE (wavecf) run on an Octatrack?: A) module README: "Not flashed" B) CHANGELOG: unit builds W1-W6 on 2026-11-07, clicks gone from W5 (I58)
- **O23** Octatrack boot fill of internal SRAM; meaning of `0x80000003`: A) KYOTI NOTES: 0x3e88 bytes copied and the rest zero-filled up to `0x80004000`; the playing pattern's Part is the slab link, and `0x80000003` "is not it" B) OCTAMAX NOTES: `.data`/`.bss` up to `0x80008000`, filled from the image tail; `0x80000003` is the active Part (verified on a unit)

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H21** (build) The Octatrack stall after a PROJECT > SYSTEM walk on Modwerk builds is Modwerk's DSP stall watchdog firing while stock itself holds the frames (USB DISK MODE), not a stock fault. Test: Make the same walk on a unit with nothing installed, then with the watchdog off.
- **H22** (build) The total freeze in octabam's demand-loader soak (I57) is the ColdFire spinning in one of the frame interrupt's waits that have no time limit, after the DSP stopped taking host words. Test: Add time limits (with a counter) to both waits and repeat the 118-switch soak.

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).

## 9. All 125 facts, best evidence first

- [hw] CPU: ColdFire MCF5445x (board photos read MCF54454VR266 or MCF5445AVR266), 32-bit big-endian. The firmware stores 264 MHz; internal bus 132 MHz (UARTs, PIT, DSPI), FlexBus 66 MHz, 24 MHz crystal. 128 MB SDRAM at `0x40000000`; NOR flash on CS0, 8 MB decode. `[hw]` — `octatrack#e4870e76` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:9](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L9) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
- [hw] Audio DSP: Freescale Symphony DSP56721, two DSP5636x cores in one chip, 200 MHz each, with no external memory. Each core has its own P memory. A 64 K-word shared window at `$030000` is reachable by both cores; P, X and Y alias there. Tracks 1-4 run on core 1 and tracks 5-8 on core 0 ("inverted from old assumptions"). Each track's FX1 and FX2 run on its own core. `[hw]` — `octatrack#c04f4cf3` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:10](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L10) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
- [hw] Storage: CompactFlash (FAT16/32) through an ATA stack (PIO task-file registers at `0x90000000`). — `octatrack#68876fc3` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:13](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L13) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
- [hw] The kernel is a proprietary preemptive microkernel (banner "ElektronOctatrack DPS-1"), not FreeRTOS. — `octatrack#410563c7` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:14](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L14) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
- [hw] 4,532 cycles per sample per core at 44.1 kHz (199.9 MHz measured). The older 4,160 / 183 MHz is retracted. — `octatrack#dbe03f43` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:17](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L17) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
- [hw] About 3,120 cycles/sample are usable for DSP work; stock takes ~1,410. — `octatrack#de2c0ab0` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L18) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
- [hw] Planning number: ~500 cycles on top of the current reverb with 4 FX1 FILTERs, ~900 with 2. One FX1 FILTER costs 192 cycles/sample. `[hw]` — `octatrack#a62bd72c` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:19](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L19) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
- [hw] Stock FX2 costs per sample (one MKII, 1.40C), dearest first: DJ EQ ~340, LO-FI ~310, SPRING ~300, CHORUS ~295, FILTER ~285, DARK ~255, PLATE ~250, PHASER ~240, EQUALIZER ~190, FLANGER ~145, COMB ~125, COMPRESSOR ~100, SPATIALIZER ~80, DELAY ~0. `[hw]` — `octatrack#a75c3fb1` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:20](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L20) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
- [hw] Words are not cycles: `move x0,a` 2 cycles, a one-word displaced `move x:(r7+$15),a` ~4, a two-word displaced ~6. Static word counts are a floor; only a burn sweep measures the ceiling. `[hw]` — `octatrack#d193db2d` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:21](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L21) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
- [hw] ColdFire access costs (one unit, 132 MHz, inside the frame interrupt, stock cache settings): register/SRAM/cache hit ~2.9 ns, uncached SDRAM store 36 ns, load 69 ns, cache miss ~80 ns, `cpushl` 46-80 ns. SRAM is 12-28x cheaper than SDRAM, and caching a transmit buffer does not help. `[hw]` — `octatrack#55ace119` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:22](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L22) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
- [hw] USB costs: one recording buffer is about 6 points of the ColdFire's frame share, USB streaming about 12. Six buffers plus streaming drop frames. `[hw]` — `octatrack#5cf972f4` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:23](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L23) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
- [hw] Every track runs `FX1 -> FX2 -> gain`. FX1 has 3,072 words of Y, FX2 16,384, which is why reverbs and delay are FX2-only. — `octatrack#b38ec80a` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:26](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L26) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / FX slots
- [hw] The card path: OS UPGRADE lists `/*.BIN` on the CF, validates, programs NOR from `0x4000` and verifies it word by word. Stock then shows "PLEASE REBOOT!" and never resets the unit itself. — `octatrack#862d5376` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L35) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
- [hw] Recovery: hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE (not TRIG 4 as on the small boxes), send the stock `.syx` over DIN MIDI. `TRIG 2` (EMPTY RESET) clears battery-backed RAM and settings, not the card. Pace about 7,460 messages at DIN rate. Filter MIDI clock on that port and merge nothing else into it: a MIDI-hub preset caused a CHECKSUM ERROR. If the unit loses sync, send again slower (60-300 ms between messages). The unit may update its bootstrap after the flash. `[hw]` — `octatrack#afda26fa` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L36) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
- [doc] [hw] How stock writes NOR (1.40C, Modwerk's reading, `[doc]` {modwerk-ot-traps}): OS UPGRADE reads the whole card file into RAM, then erases and programs NOR from there (sector erase `0x40020628`, 256-byte page program `0x400206f4`, the 37 sector starts listed at `0x400a95c0`). The layout is 8 KB boot sectors from `0x4000`, then 64 KB sectors up to `0x1f0000`. Both routines poll the chip themselves and mask interrupts only around the command bytes, so a mod can call them from a task without breaking the frame interrupt. The bootloader below `0x4000` is never written. It depacks NOR from `0x4012` without checking anything, so an image that doesn't boot is recoverable over DIN MIDI only. The startup menu's MIDI UPGRADE checks the received file, not NOR. `[hw]` (testers' units) — `octatrack#e45fd92d` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:40](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L40) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
- [hw] Don't verify a running image against its own RAM: once running, stock rewrites bytes inside its bootloader copy (`0x400e201e-0x400e2108`) and reuses the RAM after the image. Compare against digests taken before stock started. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} — `octatrack#5a68ef2e` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:45](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L45) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
- [hw] After flashing a build that changes an effect's parameter layout, old projects need their stored values stamped. A select value outside its count stalls the sequencer on first play. `[hw]` ([I28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer)) — `octatrack#e20182bb` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:46](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L46) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
- [hw] The free ROM is small: zero runs in `0x400c0000-0x400d8000` total ~8.4 KB, shared by every mod. The zero region above `0x400d8000` is the PROJECT subsystem's RAM. A menu table placed in a 15 KB zero run at `0x401087e4` crashed a unit. ([I48](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i48-a-menu-table-in-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit)) Larger code goes to a loader-copied area: octabam's loader is a stub at `0x4010fdf0`, right after the OS image, reached from the boot site. `[hw]` — `octatrack#84b1a20b` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:49](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L49) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
- [hw] DSP code that does not fit a core's P memory (ends `P:0x1fff`) runs from the shared window `P:0x30000-0x3ffff`. This was proven on a unit (PEXT probe, 2026-10-25). `[hw]` — `octatrack#41b8a0b8` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:52](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L52) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
- [hw] DSP scratch: r7 scratch `$00-$83` is the per-instance block, and `$84+` hangs the unit. Stock effects scratch `X:0x20-0xff`, and the hardware dispatcher passes the audio block at X:0. `[hw]` ([I29](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i29-dsp-scratch-at-84-and-up-hung-the-unit)) — `octatrack#4651efc4` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L53) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
- [hw] `dsp_asm` silently mis-encodes: `tfr a,b` as `rnd b`, and any `mpy` operand order it does not know as `mpysu`. `lua (rN+d),rM` takes d in -64..63 and silently wraps larger values. Labels resolve by prefix, so a new label may not have an existing label as its prefix. — `octatrack#4caacc57` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L56) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
- [hw] DSP56300 semantics: A logical op on an accumulator leaves the extension byte stale, so the next store saturates to full scale. `move a,b` limits; `tfr a,b` moves all 56 bits. A Tcc pair sharing one compare breaks with any arithmetic in between. `asr #n,a,a` shifts into a0, and Z is set only when all 56 bits are zero. Reading a0 exposes the fractional left shift that a1 hides. — `octatrack#74e879f0` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:57](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L57) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
- [hw] No `rep` in an effect's init or proc (it cannot be interrupted, and the host-command handlers need to run). No dense X work in a DMA's 8K block. — `octatrack#4caa5e48` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:63](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L63) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
- [hw] Instruction-form rule, as on the SHARC: a DSP form ships only if a stock payload runs it or a hardware probe approved it. — `octatrack#dfeff949` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:64](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L64) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
- [hw] Stock Unicorn halves every ColdFire fractional-mode multiply and adds where `msac` subtracts (the firmware runs EMAC with MACSR = 0x20), and its MAC-with-load decode has three defects. MACSR S/U is bit 6, and in fractional mode it selects 16-bit rounding. These are the same EMAC pitfalls as on the Syntakt and DN2 (rule G-series, `common/toolchain-and-emulators.md`). `[hw]` — `octatrack#a2e224b6` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:65](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L65) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
- [hw] The emulator (`ot_emu`) charges one step per instruction, with no cache or memory timing. A change can be cycle-identical in the port and several percent worse on the unit. — `octatrack#a40a70bb` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:66](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L66) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
- [hw] No EP0 reply or OUT data stage may be a whole multiple of 64 bytes. A reply of 64/128/192/256 bytes left a stale zero-length packet, and the next request returned 0 bytes (once, the unit froze). Stock leaves zero-length termination on in the EP0 OUT queue head, so a 128- or 192-byte OUT stage never completed. Send one byte less, or clear ZLT when priming. `[hw]` Rule A39. ([I5](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i5-ep0-data-stages-of-a-multiple-of-64-bytes-stall-or-freeze-stock-usb-driver)) — `octatrack#e0e5dcca` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:69](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L69) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
- [hw] About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered on a MKII: completed inside the ISR after stock's poll, or stopped part-way. Modwerk runs a 60 Hz tick that finishes a completed stage, or stalls EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits. `[hw]` ([I6](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i6-about-one-ep0-out-stage-in-50-100-goes-unanswered)) — `octatrack#77469aca` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:70](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L70) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
- [hw] DMA reads RAM, not the copyback cache. A value the CPU stores rarely stayed stale for minutes in USB replies, while values stored every frame looked live. Copy a reply through the uncached alias and send it from there. `[hw]` (Same idea as A28 on the SHARC.) ([I35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i35-usb-replies-stayed-stale-for-minutes)) — `octatrack#1ccda397` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:71](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L71) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
- [hw] A soft reset leaves the USB controller and PHY as they were: one RAM boot in about six came back with no USB until a power cycle. Stop the controller (USBCMD.RS = 0) and wait ~50 ms before resetting; that gave 20 of 20 good boots. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} ([I7](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i7-a-soft-reset-leaves-the-usb-controller-running)) — `octatrack#df6e3c52` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:72](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L72) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
- [hw] Never post key events into stock's queues directly (two crashes minutes later). Feed the panel parser its own bytes instead. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} ([I30](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i30-key-events-posted-into-stocks-queues-crashed-the-unit-minutes-later)) — `octatrack#5e94094b` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:73](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L73) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
- [hw] The Modwerk base with nothing installed shows ~42-47 % CPU. That is mostly stock's own tasks; there is no clean stock baseline yet. `[hw]` — `octatrack#a501479d` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:76](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L76) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
- [hw] An FM synth module costs ~8 points just by being installed, plus ~5 while a track plays it. Small effects cost 0.5 points or less on the ColdFire, but their DSP cost lands on their core (BBD on T6: core T5-8 went from ~44 % to 54 %). `[hw]` — `octatrack#1d165c43` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:77](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L77) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
- [hw] Uncached module code is expensive: Analog BD on one track cost ~20 points. 93 % of each call was a write lease whose owner check read the module header through the uncached alias (~0.6 µs a read). With one lease per frame it dropped to ~10 points. Lesson: take locks only where a call writes, at most once a frame, and keep uncached reads out of hot paths. `[hw]` — `octatrack#5acf3332` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:78](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L78) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
- [hw] UI-task edits can cost milliseconds: a 64-step MIDI rewrite took 3.9 ms per knob turn, mostly stock's lock-index rebuild. Updating only the own track's bits brought it to 0.5 ms. Audio frames stayed ~406-417 µs apart throughout, because it all ran on the UI task. `[hw]` — `octatrack#53717941` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:82](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L82) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
- [hw] The DSP peak meter shows the busiest single frame of a 1,024-frame window. A self-test or sync leaves it at ~99.7 % while the mean is flat and the audio fine. Judge overload by the longest frame of a real load, not the peak. `[hw]` — `octatrack#887eac41` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:83](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L83) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)

- [hw] AMP envelope: the DSP's AMP envelope restarts from zero at every trig START, so with any ATK above 0 a sound that plays across trigs drops out and fades back in, a click on every note. A ColdFire machine holds the DSP at ATK 0 / HOLD INF / REL INF and shapes AMP itself, as SYNTH MACHINE does. Measured laws (Tim Hastie): ATK is a linear ramp of 3.85 ms x 2^(ATK/8.53), at least 16 frames; REL is exponential with tau 0.295 ms x 2^(REL/8.53). `[hw]` {octabam-wavecf} (I58) — `octatrack#1573780f` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:133](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L133) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)

- [doc] Octatrack: one image for MKI and MKII (`.syx` and `.bin`); `stage` is `None`, so the in-place unpack is unsimulated. Protected `0x400de1e0-0x400e21e0`. Six hook events (sys tick, composed frame, keys, encoders, MIDI in, frame interrupt); boot site `0x4000050c`; draw gate `0x400c45b0`; image free runs `0x400c45b0-0x400c4702`, `0x400d24e0-0x400d2ce0`, `0x400d64e0-0x400d7c3c`. DSP payload A `0x136cb` bytes, payload B `0x12d05` bytes; the SPATIALIZER range P:0xaa8-0xbac (261 words) is used for mods. Arena 14,602 pages of 6,144 B. — `memory-maps#a581c1bc` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:98](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L98) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Details per device
- [doc] Other Elektron devices, from elekloader's BUILDING.md (for reference): Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII - FUNC at power-on (STARTUP menu), TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over 5-pin DIN MIDI, USB does not work. Octatrack - hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE, DIN MIDI; normal flashing from the card (PROJECT > SYSTEM > USB DISK MODE, copy the `.bin`, then PROJECT > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE, power-cycle once more before judging). Digitakt mk1 / Digitone mk1: FUNC, TRIG 4, legacy mode; the connection is not stated for these two. Per-device notes: [`analog-rytm.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md), [`digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md), [`digitone.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-building} — `recovery#ff8f0917` [hardware/common/recovery.md:37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L37) · Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)
- [doc] Both menus share one DSP dispatch table indexed by the raw id. A module on a stock effect's id replaces that effect in both slots, and removing an effect from a menu frees no space. The reclaimable pool is FX1's ten effects, 3,384 words. `[doc]` — `octatrack#d41d000c` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:27](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L27) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / FX slots
- [doc] Elektron ships the same OS as `.bin` and `.syx` (the MKI and MKII files are byte-identical for 1.40C). `.bin` = ELUP header + seed + XOR-feedback-obfuscated `[len] + ELEK(aPLib(MAIN OS))` + checksum. `.syx` = SysEx-packed ELEK container. The MAIN OS is 1,112,560 B. No cryptographic signature in any layer. `[doc]` — `octatrack#51c40b3b` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:30](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L30) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
- [doc] Validation on update returns: -1 IO, -2 not a valid OS, -3 length (more than 1 MB + 12 B), -4 checksum, -5 MK1 not allowed (version code below "0156"), -6 cannot downgrade (below "0178"). octabam images keep code 0178. `[doc]` — `octatrack#3e3f33b2` [hardware/devices/octatrack.md:34](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/octatrack.md#L34) · Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery

- [doc] LFOs: 19 waves (TRI to RND, then T1-T8); the LFO step runs in the frame interrupt for each of a track's three LFOs (24 calls a frame); phase `0`-`0x7fffff` over a cycle. - [?] Digitakt (mk1) manual: Appendix A lists sound parameters with CC numbers; high-resolution control needs NRPN, which is four CC messages (CC 99 = NRPN MSB, CC 98 = NRPN LSB, CC 6 = data MSB, CC 38 = data LSB), the MSB/LSB per parameter come from the manual; "Receive CC/NRPN" must be enabled under SETTINGS > MIDI CONFIG > PORT CONFIG. Digitone (mk1): Appendix B (MIDI implementation), ratio offsets are in a table B.3, CC 70-77 drive the MIDI track's CC value parameters. A forum user reports that the Digitakt II manual lists no CC values for the Euclidean sequencer parameters and that some Euclidean NRPNs misbehaved before OS 1.10 ("Some NRPN parameters regarding the Euclidean sequencer didn't work as intended" is in the 1.10 notes). The Octatrack is said to be the only Elektron device that answers a CC request.
